review.verdict: A clean happy-path run (1 cycle, 14 calls, 57 of 60 budget, no redirects or refusals) that passed all 8 done-when items [21], but the site cannot take a real booking or show a real number until the Requester supplies 5 inputs, and one safety warning was lost at hand-off.

identity.note: Stayed in role and closed correctly [4][21]. The CEO question bundled three decisions, Q3 option 2 has no description, and Q1 option 2 is a strawman [2]. [21] says clinical FAQ review should be tracked as an open input, but the final list in [22] omits it. The done ruling names no charter clause.

adaptation.note: One proposal, and it accepted Priority's counter within two exchanges [6][8]. It pre-cut styling and said 'Fund W1 and W2 first' [6], which is Priority and Coordination territory. Asking Priority to pick the cut invited the overreach in [7].

priority.note: Good opportunity-cost reasoning: no raise, and it named that 3 credits left cannot buy a fix [7]. It overreached by prescribing where the dentist card goes and judging the profiles part low value, which is design and relevance, not envelope. Envelope fields (stop-loss, retry limit, validity) are not visible in chat, so I cannot check them.

coordination.note: States the scheduling rule and the file lock every time and the order is correct [10][12][15]. The HOLD on W-3 in [12] was true but pointless, since W-2 was running next. It caused a release and recharge of 22 [13][16], net cost zero.

audit.note: Surfaced two real issues: empty booking recipients and unreviewed clinical advice [20]. But it chose not to route them to Adaptation because only 3 credits were left. That is Priority's call and it hides a correctable finding. Its PASS rests on code reading plus a mechanical check that did not exercise the toggle or the form output [19].

ceo.note: Three decisions, each with a reason and a named trade-off [3], and no position bias (shown-first picks 0 of 3). It did not say the brief was silent, though it was silent on all three. The reply repeats full option text and is long.

builder.note: Ran W-1, W-2 and W-3 in order on one file. Result is 40 KB, 0 external resources, no JS errors, no overflow at 360 or 1280 px [19]. Reports are short and say what changed. The only extra was two nav links in W-2 [14].

went_well: Protocol discipline: 0 redirects, 0 invalid moves, 0 validator refusals, 0 role refusals.
The Adaptation and Priority bargain closed in 2 exchanges with no Identity ruling needed [6][8].
The honesty rules held: request form with phone confirmation, 'starting from' prices, marked placeholders, Marathi labelled pending review [19][20].
Coordination stated its ordering rule and single file lock each turn, so no collisions.
problems: Clinical FAQ and emergency advice review was meant to become an open input [21] but is missing from the final handoff list [22]. This is the one health-safety warning, and the Requester will not see it.
Audit decided not to route correctable findings because of budget [20]. The 3-credit margin set by Priority [7] left no rework capacity at all.

'Done' means a template. Booking recipients, emergency number, prices and dentist names are all placeholders. The Requester pause never ran (pauses 0) because the done-when list was written so placeholders count as done [3].
Dentist profiles ended up as a card inside the services section after Priority's cut [7][8]. Audit passed it, but it is weaker than the charter's 'dentist profiles section' wording.
The ASK_CEO had a blank option and a strawman option [2], so the CEO's choice was less informed than it looks.
learnings: Change audit.md: Audit files and routes every correctable finding to Adaptation, and Priority decides funding. Evidence: [20].

Test next: a brief where the cheap cut does not exist and an audit fails with no budget left. This run never reached Identity conflict rulings, the CEO budget raise (raises: []), validator refusals or rework, so those paths are untested.
Test next: a brief where a done-when item needs a Requester-only fact, to see whether Identity pauses correctly instead of the item being designed away. Evidence: pauses 0, [3].
Test system: add a code check that every open input Identity names appears in the final open_inputs list. Evidence: [21] against [22].
Test system: validate ASK_CEO before sending (every option has text, one decision per question). Evidence: [2].

Test system: the CEO bias metric is too thin to use. n=3, and the chat shows the picked options as 'Option 3' while the log says original_pos 0 [2][3]. Fix the logging, then rerun with Identity's first option deliberately the weakest.

Test system: estimate_vs_charged is identical for all three workflows (25/25, 10/10, 22/22) because charges come from a rate card. It does not test Adaptation's estimating, and 57 spent is a charge, not a measurement.

Consider letting code advance a linear single-file queue. Coordination took 3 of 14 calls with no real decision. This is an estimate from one run, not a measured saving; keep Coordination for holds and parallel work.

Add a browser-level mechanical check: click the toggle and confirm no English text remains, and read the WhatsApp or email link target. Evidence: [19] covers only overflow, JS errors and links. Marathi quality is unchecked, and I could not see the HTML.
